content.text: I set up F4 and issued the calls along the lines mentioned. But Fedora 4 delegates, it is my understanding, node authorization operations to ModeShape, and ModeShape does not check permissions when it's updating properties, only when it's creating them (see AbstractJcrNode etc for implementation details). That's why if you try to PATCH with a reader role, your first request should fail (I say "should" because it definitely fails for me with the F4/Tomcat versions I have). ModeShape probably has performance implications or practibility considerations in mind (or perhaps this specific form of change authorization is not required by JCR). With respect to existing F4 code (especifically, modules auth, kernel, auth-rabcl) the credentials are maintained through out the session (so it's not an explicit lapse). If I have overlooked something, please feel free to point it out.
Where do you see in AbstractJcrNode that authorization is enforced on property creation?
I found references in the following:
https://github.com/ModeShape/modeshape/blob/master/modeshape-jcr/src/main/java/org/modeshape/jcr/AbstractJcrNode.java#L1670
No corresponding check in, it seems:
https://github.com/ModeShape/modeshape/blob/master/modeshape-jcr/src/main/java/org/modeshape/jcr/AbstractJcrProperty.java
The corresponding F4 calls are made in NodePropertiesTools#appendOrReplaceNodeProperty:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/utils/NodePropertiesTools.java#L64
, this certainly looks like an issue at the ModeShape level. Please make a post to the ModeShape forum asking if this is expected behavior.
https://developer.jboss.org/en/modeshape
If it is not, please be prepared to offer an integration test.
After discussing the issue on the forum, I created a JIRA ticket for Modeshape:
https://issues.jboss.org/browse/MODE-2428
Thanks,
. Can you please include a link here to the ModeShape forum thread?
Discussion:
https://developer.jboss.org/thread/252234
ModeShape has made the necessary change.
https://github.com/ModeShape/modeshape/commit/4f2ea5b7b9c88b00e7c4607cae02acd435fcaf19
The underlying modeshape issue has been merged with their master and should be included in modeshape-4.2.
This ticket should remain "in review" until modeshape-4.2 has been released and verified.
From the following e-mail it looks like ModeShape 4.2 has been released:
Hello Osman,
Thank you for participating in the ModeShape community. We've recently
released ModeShape 4.2.0.Final, and you've played an important part in
this release by helping identify and solve the following issues:
MODE-2428 [1] - ACLs not checked when updating properties
For more details about ModeShape and the new 4.2.0.Final release, please
see the project website at

https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=http-3A__jboss.org_modeshape&d=AwICaQ&c=-dg2m7zWuuDZ0MUcV7Sdqw&r=ogdRab9RQ1FK40y38qJHfVMjXs1HSR-OvLRD74IMzz8&m=SzTRCWXOvncrjdUGXpK6ssBk60fUh5r0hkbCY5WPohY&s=QeZclZcTQkVxHNCeOd0tVAgsKzlVIx6wZDdJrwzXbBA&e=
We greatly appreciate your contribution as it helped us make ModeShape
better for you as well as for other users. Please keep up the good work,
and we encourage you to continue to give us feedback and play an active
role in the ModeShape community.
Thank you very much,
--The ModeShape team
Resolved by documented ModeShape ticket.
The following ticket is a follow-on to return a more accurate status code:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1379
On a Fedora 4 instance configured to use the role-based authorization delegate, I have added an fcr:accessroles ACL to the collection /bulk13
that sets up "testuser" with just read-only access:
{ "testuser": [ "reader" ] }
Everything appears fine when I attempt to modify a container resource
under /bulk13 with PUT or POST; the PUT is rejected with a 409 and error
messages referring to insufficient permissions to modify the triples, and
the POST is rejected with a 403.
However, when I send a PATCH request with a SPARQL update query, it
succeeds (returns 204, and the resource gets updated). For example, this
command will add a triple with the predicate dc:title and the object
"foobar 2":

curl -X PATCH
http://localhost:8080/rest/bulk13/6c/16/04/6d/6c16046d-3c21-4a21-b866-febdf
cb8a61d -H 'Content-Type: application/sparql-update' -d'INSERT { <>
<http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/title> "foobar 2". } WHERE {}' -u
testuser:XXXXXX -i
Yields:

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
ETag: "ad1d4b9ed567a9bbd470de712e6c71765345d0c5"
Last-Modified: Tue, 13 Jan 2015 14:34:07 GMT
Server: Jetty(8.1.11.v20130520)
This is incorrect behavior, since testuser should not be able to modify
any resources under /bulk13, per the fcr:accessroles configuration.
Checking the effective access roles using an admin user, this is what I get:
curl 'http://localhost:8080/rest/bulk13/6c/16/04/6d/6c16046d-3c21-4a21-b866-febdfcb8a61d/fcr:accessroles?effective' -u fedoraAdmin:XXXX -i
Yields:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 23
Content-Type: application/json
Server: Jetty(8.1.11.v20130520)
{"testuser":["reader"]}
